content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your team is mobile-heavy or you only want error grouping and nothing else.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Focus** | Errors plus performance tracing, session replay, profiling, cron monitoring, logs | Error tracking, with deploy tracking and search | Error tracking and app stability (release health, stability score) |
| **SDK coverage** | Broadest: web, backend, mobile, and most languages and frameworks | Good for web and backend languages | Strong mobile (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) and common backend SDKs |
| **Grouping and triage** | Strong grouping, assignment, alert rules, and issue-to-PR workflows | Good grouping and a flexible query language | Good grouping, with a clear view of how each release affects stability |
| **Integrations** | Very wide: GitHub/GitLab, Slack, Jira, Linear, PagerDuty, and more | Solid core set (Slack, Jira, GitHub, PagerDuty) | Solid core set, with good CI and release integrations |
| **Self-hosting** | Available | Not really | Not really (on-prem only for enterprise) |
| **Pricing model** | Free tier, then a base plan plus pay-as-you-go by event; performance, replay, and other features billed separately | Free tier, then plans by event volume | Free tier, then plans by event volume; tier jumps can be steep |
| **Main downside** | Costs can grow fast once you add tracing and replay; many features to configure | Narrower product; less useful beyond errors | Weaker outside mobile and stability; owned by SmartBear |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team:**
- One tool covers errors, performance, and replay, so you avoid buying a second product later.
- The free tier is enough to evaluate on a real project, and a small team can usually start on the paid Team plan without a large bill.
- Its integrations with GitHub and Slack shorten the path from an alert to a fix.

**When to pick something else:**
- **Bugsnag** if most of your code is native mobile and release stability is what you care about most.
- **Rollbar** if you only need error tracking, want a simpler tool, and expect high event volume where its per-event pricing may come out cheaper.

**Before you decide:**
- Pricing and free-tier limits change often. I'm working from memory, so check the current pricing pages. Then estimate your monthly error volume (events, not unique errors) and what you'd pay at 2–3x that volume, since that's where the bills diverge.
- Run two tools on one service for two weeks if you can. Look at how well each groups your real errors and how noisy the alerts are.

I can search for current pricing if you want exact numbers, or draft a short evaluation checklist for the trial.
